questions.question_text:
A shoe shop records the colour of each pair sold one afternoon:
navy, navy, tan, black, navy, tan, black, navy
Which measure of centre should be used, and what is its value?

options.text: The mode, and it is navy.
The mode, and it is tan.
options.why: Miscounts the colours; tan was sold twice while navy was sold four times.

options.text: The median, and it is navy.
options.why: Colours have no meaningful numerical order, so a middle value cannot be found.

options.text: The mean, and it is navy.
options.why: The mean needs values that can be added and divided, and colours cannot be.

questions.solution_text:
Colours cannot be added or placed in numerical order, so only the mode can be used.
Navy was sold four times, more often than any other colour, so the mode is navy.

options.text: The median, $\$49\,000$

options.why: Uses the mean even though the $\$180\,000$ salary lifts it above five of the six salaries.

options.text: The median, $\$50\,000$
options.why: Takes a single middle salary instead of the mean of the two middle salaries of an even-sized set.
Every salary occurs once, so this data has no mode at all.

questions.solution_text:
The salary of $\$180\,000$ is an outlier that pulls the mean upwards.
$\overline{x} = \frac{420}{6}$
$= \$70\,000$
$\text{Median} = \frac{48 + 50}{2}$
$= \$49\,000$
The mean is higher than five of the six salaries, so the median of $\$49\,000$ best represents a typical salary.

questions.question_text: Six houses in a suburb sold for $\$690\,000$, $\$700\,000$, $\$710\,000$, $\$730\,000$, $\$740\,000$ and $\$750\,000$. Which measure of centre is the most appropriate to report, and why?

options.text: The mean, because no price sits far from the others and it uses the value of every price.
The median, because a set of house prices is always distorted by outliers.
options.why: Assumes every set of house prices contains an outlier, but these prices are evenly spread.

options.text: The median, because half of the houses sold for less than that price.
options.why: Restates what a median is instead of giving a reason to prefer it to the mean here.

options.text: The mode, because it is the price that occurs most often.
options.why: Every price occurs once, so this data has no mode.

questions.solution_text:
$\overline{x} = \frac{4\,320\,000}{6}$
$= \$720\,000$
No price sits far from the others, so there is no outlier to distort the mean.
The mean of $\$720\,000$ is the most appropriate measure, because it uses the value of every price.

questions.question_text: A uniform shop sold these sizes of school shirts in one day: $4$, $5$, $6$, $6$, $7$, $7$, $7$ and $9$. The owner wants to know which size to order more of. Which measure of centre is the most useful?

options.text: The mode, $7$
The mean, $6.375$
options.why: The shop does not stock a size $6.375$, so this figure cannot be ordered.

options.text: The median, $6.5$
options.why: A size $6.5$ is not stocked, and the median does not say which size sold most often.

options.text: The mode, $6$
options.why: Treats $6$ as the most frequent size, but $6$ occurs twice while $7$ occurs three times.

questions.solution_text:
$4, 5, 6, 6, 7, 7, 7, 9$
$\text{Mode} = 7$
The mode is the most useful measure, because it names a size the shop actually stocks and it is the size that sold most often.

questions.question_text: The yearly salaries of six staff, in thousands of dollars, are $38$, $38$, $38$, $62$, $70$ and $74$. Why is the mode a poor measure of centre for this data?

options.text: The mode is the lowest salary, so it does not sit near the middle of the data.
The mode is distorted by the outlier of $\$74\,000$.
options.why: The mode is never affected by outliers, and $\$74\,000$ is not far from the other salaries.

options.text: The mode cannot be used, because the data is numerical rather than categorical.
options.why: The mode can be found for numerical data; it is the mean and median that fail for categories.

options.text: The mode cannot be found, because three of the salaries are equal.
options.why: Three equal salaries are what make $38$ the most frequent value, which is exactly the mode.

questions.solution_text:
$\text{Mode} = 38$
The mode of $\$38\,000$ is the lowest salary in the dataset, and three of the six staff earn much more than it.
A measure of centre should sit near the middle of the data, so the mode is a poor choice here.

questions.question_text: Seven houses in a street sold for, in thousands of dollars, $540$, $560$, $580$, $950$, $950$, $950$ and $970$. Why is the median not a central value for this data?

options.text: The median, $\$950\,000$, has only one price above it, so it sits near the top of the data.
The median, $\$950\,000$, is pulled up by the outlier of $\$970\,000$.
options.why: The median is not distorted by a single large value, and $\$970\,000$ is close to the other high prices.

options.text: The median, $\$540\,000$, is lower than every other price, so it sits at the bottom.
options.why: Takes the smallest price as the median instead of the fourth of the seven ordered prices.

options.text: The median cannot be used, because there is an odd number of prices.
options.why: With an odd number of values the median is simply the middle one, so it can always be found.

questions.solution_text:
$540, 560, 580, 950, 950, 950, 970$
There are $7$ prices, so the median is the $4$th one.
$\text{Median} = \$950\,000$
Only $\$970\,000$ is above the median, and two more prices equal it, so the median sits at the top of the data rather than near its middle.

questions.question_text: Six houses sold for $\$610\,000$, $\$620\,000$, $\$640\,000$, $\$660\,000$, $\$690\,000$ and $\$2\,180\,000$. An agent advertises an average price of $\$900\,000$. Which measure of centre is the agent using?

options.text: The mean
The median
options.why: The median of these six prices is $\$650\,000$, not the advertised $\$900\,000$.

options.text: The mode
options.why: Every price occurs once, so this data has no mode to advertise.

options.text: The range
options.why: The range of $\$1\,570\,000$ measures spread rather than an average.

questions.solution_text:
$\overline{x} = \frac{5\,400\,000}{6}$
$= \$900\,000$
$\text{Median} = \frac{640\,000 + 660\,000}{2}$
$= \$650\,000$
The advertised figure matches the mean, so the agent is using the mean.

questions.question_text: Which of these is a disadvantage of using the median as a measure of centre?

options.text: It ignores the size of the values on either side of it, so it may not be a central value.
It is distorted by a single very large value in the dataset.
options.why: That is a disadvantage of the mean; a single large value barely moves the median.

options.text: It cannot be found when the dataset has an even number of values.
options.why: With an even number of values the median is the mean of the two middle values.

options.text: It cannot be found when the dataset contains negative values.
options.why: The median can be found for any numerical data, including negative values.

questions.solution_text:
The median is only the middle of the ordered data, so it takes no account of how large or small the other values are.
It can therefore sit at the top or the bottom of the data instead of near its middle, as in $0, 1, 1, 5, 5, 5, 5$, where the median is $5$.

questions.question_text: In a company, $10$ employees each earn $\$46\,000$ a year and the $2$ directors each earn $\$370\,000$ a year. Which measure would the company quote to make its pay look high, and which better describes a typical wage?

options.text: Quote the mean, $\$100\,000$; a typical wage is the median, $\$46\,000$.
Quote the median, $\$46\,000$; a typical wage is the mean, $\$100\,000$.
options.why: Swaps the two; the mean is the larger figure here because the directors' pay lifts it.

options.text: Quote the mean, $\$208\,000$; a typical wage is the median, $\$46\,000$.
options.why: Averages $\$46\,000$ and $\$370\,000$ instead of using the total of all $12$ salaries.

options.text: Quote the mean, $\$100\,000$; a typical wage is the mode, $\$370\,000$.
options.why: The most frequent salary is $\$46\,000$, earned by ten people, not the directors' pay.

questions.solution_text:
$\overline{x} = \frac{1\,200\,000}{12}$
$= \$100\,000$
$\text{Median} = \$46\,000$
The company would quote the mean of $\$100\,000$, because the two large salaries lift it above every employee's pay.
The median of $\$46\,000$ better describes a typical wage, because it is what ten of the twelve people actually earn.
